title: Mangrove Forests Are Growing Back Worldwide
paragraphs: Mangroves are trees that grow in salty water along warm coasts. They protect villages from storms and waves, and they store a lot of carbon. For many years, people cut them down to make space for farms and fish ponds.
A new study in the journal Science used satellite pictures from 1984 to 2023. The scientists saw that the world lost nearly 3,000 square kilometres of mangroves until 2010.

After 2010, the trend turned around. Mangroves grew by nearly 2,000 square kilometres, mostly in Asia, Australia and South America. About two thirds of the growth came from mangroves moving into new places. The rest came from people helping old forests grow back. The lead scientist says people should not relax, because some places still lose forest.

questions.q: What did the scientists use for their study?
How much did mangroves grow after 2010?
Where did most of the growth happen?
questions.a: In Asia, Australia and South America.
